text.p: McDonald's Corp, responding to feedback from franchisees and customers, on Tuesday it was adjusting its Campaign 55 promotion, which began in early April.
Campaign 55 involves several components including pricing and fast service.

McDonald's said it decided on what it termed a "mid-course correction" in the pricing offerings of Campaign 55. The company said it decided to continue its popular breakfast My Size Meals at 55 cents and phase out the 55 cent rotating special meal offerings at lunch and dinner.

"While customer response to My Size Meal offerings at breakfast was outstanding, customer response over the first six weeks of the lunch and dinner regular-menu components of the value initiative was not up to our expectations," said Richard Starmann, McDonald's senior vice president, in a statement.
McDonald's had proposed that franchisees offer customers coupons for free sandwiches if orders failed to arrive within 55 seconds of being placed.

"It was something that we considered, but it wasn't scrapped because it was never a plan that we had implemented," McDonald's spokesman Chuck Ebeling said, adding that the company did not receive the support from franchisees it felt was necessary to implement the guarantee.
McDonald's plans some marketing programs focusing on speed and accuracy of service, possibly this summer, but the marketing would not involve a service guarantee, he said.

McDonald's said it would increase advertising support of the Campaign 55 breakfast menu. The "My McDonald's" advertising theme, introduced also in early April, will continue. Leo Burnett Co. handles the advertising campaign.
"We made it clear from the start that we would monitor performance closely and make adjustments along the way as needed," Starmann said.
